# Results — Study 880 (Aggregate Short Interest)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test — Rapach,
Ringgenberg & Zhou (2016): the **market-wide** short-interest index is "arguably the
strongest known predictor" of the aggregate equity return, with a **negative** slope (high
aggregate SI → lower forward market return). We rebuild the index from the **FINRA
consolidated short-interest** file and regress forward SPY returns on its detrended level.
Offline & deterministic once cached; run `python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every
number. Sample as-of 2026-06-30 (the last complete settlement month; the in-progress July
print is dropped). Fingerprint `4ab933bfbc01` (aggregate index frame).*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real SI tape | **FINRA Consolidated Short Interest** (official bi-monthly settlement-date report), pulled per-name from the public FINRA Query API (`api.finra.org/data`, no key), **50-name liquid US panel**, **205 settlement dates** 2017-12-29 → 2026-06-30 |
| Aggregate index | equal-weight **cross-sectional mean days-to-cover** across the panel per settlement date (median **50** names/date); the *short-interest ratio* in the volume sense |
| Predictor | **detrended log index** (residual of `log(index)` on a linear time trend, RRZ step), standardised to unit variance — high = shorts crowded relative to trend |
| Return tape | **SPY** daily total-return (`auto_adjust=True`, yfinance), forward log return measured on the settlement grid |
| Execution / lag | one documented lag: a settlement-`t` print (published ~8 business days later) is acted on at the **next** settlement `t+1`; the forward return runs `t+1 → t+1+H` |
| Statistics | OLS slope with **Newey-West (HAC, 6-lag)** *t*; R²; a high/low tercile Welch *t*; a 5,000-draw permutation placebo; a two-era cut; a costed timing overlay; a 20-seed synthetic control |

**Availability / proxy honesty — named on the Signal axis.** Aggregate short interest is
**not** a daily series: FINRA settles and publishes it only **twice a month** (24/yr) with an
~8-day reporting lag, so the whole sample is 205 bi-monthly prints since 2017-12. FINRA
publishes no shares-outstanding, so the index is a **days-to-cover** average — a
short-interest ratio in the *volume* sense — not the *shares-outstanding* ratio of the
original paper. The panel is **current-membership mega-caps** (a survivor set); mega-cap
days-to-cover is a coarse proxy for the market-wide index RRZ built on all NYSE/AMEX/NASDAQ
names over 1973–2014. All magnitudes are therefore an approximation, and the sample is short
and mostly a bull market.

## The headline — forward-SPY-return regression on the detrended index

RRZ predict a **negative** slope. Horizons are in bi-monthly settlement periods (~0.5 mo each):

| horizon | n | slope (bps per 1σ) | Newey-West *t* | R² | forward mean |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **1 (~0.5 mo)** — headline | 203 | **−17.2** | **−0.66** | 0.28% | +55 bps |
| 2 (~1.0 mo) | 202 | −12.8 | −0.26 | 0.08% | +110 bps |
| 3 (~1.5 mo) | 201 | −35.5 | −0.50 | 0.41% | +168 bps |
| 6 (~3.0 mo) | 198 | −101.3 | −0.70 | 2.07% | +338 bps |

The slope carries the **correct RRZ sign** — negative at *every* horizon — but is **nowhere
near significant**: |NW *t*| ≤ 0.70 and R² ≤ 0.4% at the monthly horizon. The famous
predictor does not replicate on this modern, mega-cap, days-to-cover index.

## High vs low short-interest tercile — forward one-period SPY return

| bucket | forward mean | n |
|---|--:|--:|
| low-SI tercile | +67 bps | 68 |
| high-SI tercile | +21 bps | 68 |
| **Welch *t* (high − low)** | **−0.75** | — |

Directionally consistent (crowded-short periods earn a little less) but a coin-flip.

## Placebo — is the (weak, right-signed) slope a lucky alignment?

Permute the forward-return vector against the index, 5,000 draws (left-tail test on RRZ's
negative slope):

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| observed slope | −17.22 bps |
| placebo mean (sd) | −0.13 bps (22.48) |
| left-tail *p* (P[permuted ≤ observed]) | **0.217** |

The observed slope sits only ~0.8σ into the left tail — indistinguishable from noise.

## Robustness — two eras (split 2022-06-01)

| era | n | slope | NW *t* | R² |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 2017-12 → 2022-05 | 107 | −21.4 bps | −0.60 | 0.50% |
| 2022-06 → 2026-06 | 96 | −13.2 bps | −0.34 | 0.13% |

Both halves agree in **sign** (negative, the RRZ direction) but **neither is significant** —
a consistent-but-flat non-result, not a one-era artefact.

## The timer — can you get paid for it?

De-risk to cash when shorts are crowded (`sii > 0`); one-way cost × NAV per switch:

| one-way cost | overlay net | annualised | Sharpe | switches | buy-and-hold |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **1 bp** | +35.3 bps/period | **+8.5%/yr** | 0.71 | 70 | +13.2%/yr |
| **5 bps** | +34.0 bps/period | **+8.2%/yr** | 0.68 | 70 | +13.2%/yr |

The overlay **underperforms buy-and-hold** at any cost — a weak signal used to sit out of a
bull market just gives up equity premium. **Mirage.**

## Synthetic positive control — the machinery is unbiased

Deterministic seeded bi-monthly index + daily SPY-like price with a planted negative
detrended-SI → forward-return relation (`edge > 0`); null at `edge = 0`. No network.

| world | slope NW *t* |
|---|--:|
| null (`edge = 0`), **20 seeds** | mean **+0.47** (sd 0.72), **\|t\| ≥ 2 in 1/20** (over 100 seeds mean +0.02 — unbiased) |
| planted (`edge = 0.015`, seed 880) | **−4.10** (β = −103.8 bps/σ, R² = 7.0%) |

The regression recovers a *planted* RRZ relation cleanly and does not fire on the null — so
the flat real-tape result is a genuine non-finding, not a broken engine. *(A faithful-engine
power check only — never cited in support of the real-tape stamp.)*

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** The Rapach-Ringgenberg-Zhou aggregate-short-interest predictor does
  **not** replicate on a 2017–2026 FINRA-built, 50-mega-cap, days-to-cover index. The
  forward-SPY-return slope has the **right sign** (−17.2 bps/σ, negative at all four horizons,
  negative in both eras) but is **statistically absent**: NW *t* = **−0.66**, R² = **0.28%**,
  placebo *p* = 0.22, tercile Welch *t* = −0.75. The 20-seed synthetic control fires on the
  planted world and stays quiet on the null, so this is a true non-finding. The likely
  reasons — a **days-to-cover mega-cap proxy** (not the paper's market-wide shares-outstanding
  ratio), a **short, mostly-bull sample**, and a **bi-monthly** cadence — are named on the
  Signal axis, but the honest read on *this* tape is: claimed edge absent.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** The de-risk-on-crowded-shorts overlay earns **+8.5%/yr** net (1 bp)
  versus **+13.2%/yr** buy-and-hold — a weak, wrong-way-for-a-bull-market timing rule that
  destroys return rather than adding it.
